ranking.checkpoint: ggml-org/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF Q4_K_M (19.13 GiB; about 8-9 GiB of experts in RAM)
ranking.reason: Best overall agentic coder that runs here, with independent support: NVIDIA's same-harness NeMo Evaluator table gives SWE-bench Verified 70.12 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 44.38, the highest independent numbers in the set (vendor numbers are 73.4 / TB2.0 51.5). Released 2026-04, Apache-2.0. Thinking can be toggled per request, so one deployment covers both lists. Native Qwen3-Coder XML tool calls go through llama.cpp's dedicated parser. vLLM is blocked on 16 GB: no checkpoint is under 19.4 GiB, and UVA expert offload is undone by #66264. Corrections applied: the VRAM margin at --n-cpu-moe 20 is only 0.3-0.8 GiB, so plan for 21-22. The card's general thinking sampling is temp 1.0 with presence_penalty 1.5; temp 0.6 is the precise-coding preset. Use the server-cuda (12.8.1) image, because server-cuda13 sets NVIDIA_REQUIRE_CUDA>=13.5 with no GeForce brand clause and is likely refused. Decode speed is bounded by DDR5 and has not been measured. Add -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 if the laptop GPU hangs (#27330).

ranking.checkpoint: unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF UD-Q3_K_XL (13.15 GB), or UD-IQ4_XS at about 48k context
ranking.reason: Newest Qwen (2026-08-14, Apache-2.0) and the strongest model that fits fully in VRAM. Artificial Analysis measured Terminal-Bench 2.1 at 79.8% xhigh / 65.2% medium, but that was BF16 through the Alibaba API, and AA's Terminal-Bench 4.0 is only 5.6%. Ranked below Qwen3.6 because it runs only at 3-bit, the quality loss at that quant is unmeasured, and context tops out around 64-88k against a 262k native window. It does not fit vLLM: even the smallest AutoRound build (15.59 GiB) exceeds the budget. Corrections applied: llama.cpp #27330 (CUDA-graph GPU hang) was reproduced with this model on Ubuntu 26.04 and driver 595.99.02, the exact host stack, so GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 is mandatory. The q8_0 KV decode penalty is contested (#27623; fix PR #31802 still open). The Ollama default tag (18 GB) spills to CPU and is not byte-identical to 27b-q4_K_M. Set reasoning_effort medium in OpenCode; the default xhigh is verbose. Thinking can be toggled.

ranking.name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B IT
ranking.runtime: llama.cpp llama-server in Docker (ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407), text only (no mmproj), -ngl 99 -c 65536 -np 1 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --jinja, temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 64. For 128k, add --n-cpu-moe 6. Alternative: Ollama gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat with num_ctx 65536, flash attention and q8_0 KV.
ranking.reason: Best Gemma for agentic coding. Released 2026-04-02, Apache-2.0. Independent NVIDIA same-harness results are SWE-bench Verified 57.4 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 37.2, above gpt-oss-20b and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and second only to the Qwen MoE. Thinking can be toggled (off by default, so enable it per request). It runs fully on GPU at 64k. Corrections applied: F16 KV at 64k does not fit (subtraction error); q8_0 gives about 79-129k. For 256k you need about --n-cpu-moe 9. The Ollama blob is not byte-identical to Google's file. The 26B does not fit in vLLM. Risks: llama.cpp #29655 (open) reports unstable streamed write/edit tool arguments for this exact model, and other harnesses give much lower SWE-bench (Qwen scaffold 17.4, KAT 35.8). Test it with OpenCode's edit tool before relying on it.

ranking.reason: Best non-thinking model with tool calling. Released 2026-02-03, Apache-2.0. Independent Artificial Analysis results are tau2 79.5% and Terminal-Bench 2.1 38.2%; vendor SWE-bench Verified is 70.6-71.3 across three scaffolds. It is non-thinking, which avoids OpenCode #55378 (reasoning-only empty turns) and gives fast agent loops. Costs: about 26 GiB of the roughly 40 GiB free RAM, decode bound by DDR5, and no vLLM path. Corrections applied: VRAM at 131k with q8_0 KV is about 13.2 GiB plus CUDA context, not 14.3; 262k is marginal. The official Q4_K_M is 45.09 GiB. Open #28581: IQ-type tensors give garbage output on sm_120 when built with nvcc 13.2.0/13.2.1. Verify output quality on the chosen image on first run, and fall back to UD-Q3_K_XL or Q4 if it is wrong. The server-cuda13 image is also likely refused on GeForce.

ranking.checkpoint: openai/gpt-oss-20b (MXFP4 native, 12.82 GiB) for vLLM; ggml-org/gpt-oss-20b-GGUF MXFP4 (11.28 GiB) for llama.cpp
ranking.reason: Covers the must-have gpt-oss family. It is the family's current release, but it dates from 2025-08-05, outside the 12-month window. Apache-2.0. Thinking is always on (low/medium/high). It is the only official checkpoint that runs fully in vLLM with 64k context. Decode was measured at about 205 t/s on a desktop RTX 5080 with llama.cpp. Agentic quality is middling on independent evidence: NVIDIA same-harness SWE-bench Verified 52.44 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 15.17, against the vendor's 60.7 at high effort. Corrections applied: on sm_120 FA2 has no sinks, and TRITON_ATTN supports sinks plus FP8 KV, so force TRITON_ATTN. That also avoids the FlashInfer async race #61239, whose fix is not in v0.33.0. vLLM accepts only tool_choice=auto, and #65770 (HTTP 500 after a malformed tool name) is open. A context of 65536 at 0.92 does not fit; it needs 0.95 with FP8 KV.

ranking.reason: Best runnable Nemotron. Released 2026-08-11 under OpenMDW-1.1 (permissive). Thinking can be toggled, and KV is very cheap (6 KiB/token), so 128-256k context is easy. Quality is mid-tier, and every number is NVIDIA-run, though in a single harness shared with competitors: SWE-bench Verified 51.56 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 24.58, against Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at 70.12 / 44.38. It ranks above the smaller Nemotrons (3 Nano 4B, Bolt E4B) because NVIDIA positions those for edge assistants and publishes no coding scores for them. Corrections applied: force_nonempty_content is a no-op in llama.cpp (only vLLM's nemotron_v3 parser reads it), so drop it from the command. --moe-cache-mib is a VRAM cache, not host memory. The vLLM UVA offload sketch is refuted by #66264. It has not been run on any 16 GB card.

ranking.reason: Second vLLM-native pick, with an official vendor quant that avoids the NVFP4 FlashInfer JIT RAM spike. Released 2026-06-03, Apache-2.0. Thinking can be toggled, and it runs fully on GPU at 128k. Independent Artificial Analysis Terminal-Bench 2.1 is 27.3% with reasoning, above gpt-oss-20b's 15.17, though from a different harness. Correction applied: v0.33.0 reserves 2 x 2048 in-flight tokens of sliding-window KV under default async scheduling (#49878), which lowers the BF16 maximum from about 193k. That is why FP8 KV (Triton attention, forced for Gemma 4 anyway) or about 98k BF16 is recommended. Open gemma4 parser bugs remain (#54256 dropped calls after the thought channel, #66430, #50889), so always pass both parsers and test tool loops.

ranking.reason: Third vLLM option and the strongest small model on paper, with huge context headroom: 262k fits even with FP8 KV. Released 2026-08, MIT tag (the linked LICENSE file returns 404). Thinking can be toggled, with native Qwen3-Coder XML tools. Placement rests only on vendor claims from an HF org that is not verified and names no team: SWE-bench Verified 70.6 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 46.2 for a 9B model. No independent run exists, so it ranks below models with independent evidence. It replaces Qwen3.5-9B (its base), whose independent-ish numbers are SWE-V 53-60 and TB2.1 19-27. Qwen3.5-9B is the conservative swap if vendor-only claims are unacceptable. Corrections applied: FP8 KV routes to FlashInfer, not FA2, on sm_120, so BF16 KV at 131072 is recommended to stay on the default path. #54331 (hybrid-GDN NVFP4 crash under sustained load with CUDA graphs) is relevant; fall back to --enforce-eager if it appears. The template reads reasoning_content while vLLM emits 'reasoning'.

ranking.reason: Adds a fourth lab (Z.ai) and an MIT license. Released 2026-01-19, thinking can be toggled, and llama.cpp ships a tested template for it. Independent Artificial Analysis Terminal-Bench Hard is 22% with reasoning, comparable to Gemma 4 12B; vendor SWE-bench Verified is 59.2. Chosen over Laguna XS 2.1 and KAT-Coder-V2.5-Dev, which have only vendor numbers and trail or contest their Qwen3.6 base, and over Devstral Small 2. Devstral is non-thinking, with an independently checked SWE-bench Verified of 56.4, but on 16 GB it reaches only 32k context with q8_0 KV and needs q4_0 KV for 64k. Corrections applied: --n-cpu-moe 17 moves only 16 MoE layers because layer 0 is dense, so use 18-20. The vLLM AutoRound plus UVA offload route is refuted by #66264. Avoid vLLM's glm47 parser anyway (#67684, #60703, #67471 are open). AA marks the model deprecated in favour of GLM-5.

ranking.name: DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B
ranking.runtime: llama.cpp llama-server in Docker (ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407), -c 65536 -ngl 99 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa on --reasoning-format deepseek, temp 0.6 / top_p 0.95; or Ollama deepseek-r1:8b. Chat and reasoning only, with no tool calling.
ranking.reason: Included only to cover the must-have DeepSeek family. It is the only DeepSeek checkpoint that runs on 16 GB (all V3.2/V4 models are hundreds of billions of parameters). It belongs on the 'thinking, no tool calling' list, not as an OpenCode agent backend. The official template never renders tool definitions, the tool tokens are absent from the vocab, vLLM's deepseek_v3 parser raises at init, and vLLM marks the R1 series as not supporting tools. Artificial Analysis independently measured tau2 0% and Terminal-Bench Hard 1.5%. It is always thinking (an off switch exists only in Ollama), MIT-licensed, and from 2025-05-29, outside the window. Corrections applied: if vLLM is used, '--quantization fp8' is deprecated in v0.33.0 (use fp8_per_tensor), and FP8 KV routes to FlashInfer on sm_120. Use it for reasoning or Q&A beside an agent model, not for OpenCode tool loops.

notes:
Coverage of the 10: the must-have families are Qwen (#1, #2, #4), Gemma (#3, #7), gpt-oss (#5), Nemotron (#6) and DeepSeek (#10). Other labs: Ornith (#8, a Qwen3.5 fine-tune) and Z.ai (#9). Runtimes: vLLM v0.33.0 is primary for #5, #7 and #8 (gpt-oss-20b, Gemma 4 12B QAT W4A16, Ornith NVFP4-W4A16), the only configurations that fit the 14.65 GiB vLLM budget with at least 64k context. llama.cpp is used for every MoE larger than VRAM (#1, #3, #4, #6, #9), for #2 and for #10, with Ollama as the simpler fallback for several. Thinking: always on for #5 and #10. Toggle for #1, #2, #3, #6, #7, #8 and #9, which also serve as non-thinking with the toggle off. Natively non-thinking with tools: #4 Qwen3-Coder-Next. No tool calling: #10. Licenses: Apache-2.0 (#1, #2, #3, #4, #5, #7), OpenMDW-1.1 (#6), MIT (#8 tag only, #9, #10).

Cross-cutting corrections every command needs:
(a) Use ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda (CUDA 12.8.1), pinned to server-cuda-b12407. The server-cuda13 image that most records used sets NVIDIA_REQUIRE_CUDA cuda>=13.5 with no GeForce brand clause and is likely refused on driver 595 (CUDA 13.2). The tags server-cuda13-b12418 and server-cuda-b12418 do not exist.
(b) Add -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 when hangs appear (#27330, reproduced on this exact driver).
(c) --no-mmap and --mlock were removed; use -lm.
(d) Set -np 1.
(e) In OpenCode v2.3.0, declare capabilities.tools=true; built-in vLLM discovery starts with tools off. Set limit.context to match the server, and set maxTokensField max_tokens for Ollama.
(f) Install the NVIDIA Container Toolkit first (CDI recommended on this systemd-cgroup host), and cap container RAM with --memory, because heavy does not cap dockerd containers.
(g) UVA expert offload in vLLM v0.33.0 is undone for Marlin-repacked MoE (#66264), so no MoE larger than VRAM is ranked on vLLM.

Placements that rest only on vendor claims: #8 Ornith (no independent data at all) and part of #2 (the AA figure is BF16 through the API, not the Q3 GGUF). #6 Nemotron Lightning numbers are NVIDIA-run, though in a harness shared with competitors.

Runners-up not ranked:
- Qwen3.5-9B: a conservative vLLM swap for #8.
- Devstral Small 2 24B: non-thinking, independently checked SWE-V 56.4, but only 32k context at q8_0 KV on 16 GB.
- Laguna XS 2.1 and KAT-Coder-V2.5-Dev: vendor-only numbers that trail or contest Qwen3.6.
- MiMo-V2.6-Distill: an SFT research checkpoint, and its tool-argument format is contested.
- Granite 4.2 8B and Ministral 3: weak independent agentic scores.
- Nemotron 3 Nano 4B and Bolt E4B, and Gemma 4 E4B: edge models, useful only as title/sub-agent helpers or for smoke-testing the stack.
- Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B: outside the window, and an independent SWE-V of 31.8.
- gpt-oss-120b: needs about 50 GiB of RAM against about 40 GiB free.

Nothing here was run on the machine. All fit and speed figures are source-backed arithmetic or inferred.
